title: "Hands-on: ignore, archive, and LFS"

# Hands-on: ignore, archive, and LFS

Build a disposable `desk-api` repository to see three independent decisions: which untracked files Git offers to add, which committed files enter an archive, and which committed content is stored as an LFS pointer. You need Git, a POSIX shell and `tar`; the final section also needs Git LFS. No server is required.

## Create the repository

Run the block in a terminal. It creates a new temporary directory, prints its path, and configures an identity only in that repository.

```sh
lab_dir=$(mktemp -d)
printf 'Lab directory: %s\n' "$lab_dir"
cd "$lab_dir" || exit 1
git init -q
git config user.name 'Lab Author'
git config user.email 'lab@example.test'
mkdir notes
printf 'application source\n' > app.txt
printf 'maintainer notes\n' > notes/internal.txt
printf '*.log\n' > .gitignore
printf '/notes export-ignore\n' > .gitattributes
printf 'local diagnostic\n' > debug.log
git add .gitignore .gitattributes app.txt notes/internal.txt
git commit -q -m 'Create desk-api'
```

Check the rules and the snapshot:

```sh
git status --short --ignored
git check-ignore -v debug.log
git ls-files
git archive --format=tar HEAD > "$lab_dir/release.tar"
tar -tf "$lab_dir/release.tar"
```

`debug.log` appears as ignored and `check-ignore` identifies the matching rule. It is absent from `git ls-files` because it was never added. The archive contains `app.txt`, `.gitignore`, and `.gitattributes`, but not `notes/internal.txt`: the notes are tracked yet have the archive attribute. `release.tar` itself is untracked and absent from the archive because it was not in the commit. Output order can vary.

Now append `/app.txt export-ignore` to `.gitattributes` without committing it, and compare:

```sh
printf '/app.txt export-ignore\n' >> .gitattributes
git archive HEAD | tar -tf -
git archive --worktree-attributes HEAD | tar -tf -
```

The first listing still contains `app.txt`; the second omits it. Commit the attribute change if you want it to apply when archiving this new commit without `--worktree-attributes`. For the rest of the lab, restore the original rule with `git restore .gitattributes` (this discards only the uncommitted change made in this exercise).

## Add an LFS asset

If `git lfs version` reports that LFS is unavailable, install the distribution's `git-lfs` package first. Run this section in the disposable repository, not in a project containing valuable hook customizations. `--local` confines filter configuration to this repository.

```sh
git lfs install --local
git lfs track '*.bin'
printf 'sample payload for the lab\n' > sample.bin
git add .gitattributes sample.bin
git commit -m 'Store sample asset with LFS'
git lfs ls-files
git show HEAD:sample.bin
cat sample.bin
```

The sample is deliberately small so the lab works quickly; real projects select files for practical reasons such as size and change frequency. The `git show` output is a pointer beginning with `version https://git-lfs.github.com/spec/v1`; `cat` prints the payload. Git stores the pointer in the commit, while the LFS payload is in local storage. No remote upload has happened. A real collaboration setup requires an LFS-capable remote and a successful push of both kinds of objects.

## Practice questions

1. If `debug.log` had already been tracked before the ignore rule was added, would the rule stop tracking it?
2. If you add a secret to `notes/internal.txt`, does `export-ignore` make that secret safe to commit?
3. After the LFS commit, is the payload contained in the normal Git blob printed by `git show`?
4. What changes if you edit the working copy but archive `HEAD`?

**Answers:** (1) No; ignore rules normally apply to untracked paths. (2) No; the secret remains in Git history and clones. (3) No; that blob is the pointer, and the payload is in LFS storage. (4) The archive still reads the committed snapshot; uncommitted content is absent. If `--worktree-attributes` is used, working-tree attributes can alter selection, but the archived file contents still come from the specified tree.

When finished, leave with `cd`. The printed lab directory can be removed when you no longer need it.
